https://tutorialsdojo.com/amazon-sagemaker/

question: Algoritmos integrados de SageMaker - ¿cual es el uso principal de Principal Component Analysis (PCA)?
options: Reduccion de dimensionalidad preservando la mayor varianza posible
Deteccion no supervisada de anomalias en series de tiempo
Prediccion de un valor continuo a partir de features tabulares
Descubrimiento de temas latentes en colecciones de texto
correct_text: Reduccion de dimensionalidad preservando la mayor varianza posible
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - reduccion de dimensionalidad preservando varianza.

Definicion: PCA proyecta los datos sobre componentes principales (ejes ortogonales) para reducir dimensiones conservando la mayor varianza; sirve para extraccion de features o visualizacion.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Anomalias en series de tiempo: eso lo hace Random Cut Forest (RCF).
  • Predecir valor continuo tabular: eso es regresion, tarea de Linear Learner o XGBoost.
  • Temas latentes en texto: eso lo hace NTM (Neural Topic Model) o LDA.
Exam tipPCA = reducir dimensiones. RCF = anomalias. Linear Learner/XGBoost = regresion/clasificacion. NTM/LDA = temas de texto.

Random Cut Forest (RCF) Algorithm
Principal Component Analysis (PCA) Algorithm
Amazon SageMaker IP Insights
Incorrect
Amazon SageMaker IP Insights is an unsupervised learning algorithm specifically designed to analyze usage patterns of IPv4 addresses. It captures associations between these IP addresses and various entities, such as user IDs or account numbers. For instance, you can use it to detect a user attempting to log into a web service from an anomalous IP address. Additionally, it helps identify accounts that create computing resources from unexpected IP addresses. Trained IP Insight models can be deployed as real-time prediction endpoints or used for batch processing.

amazon-sagemaker-ip-insights

By analyzing historical network traffic logs, Amazon SageMaker IP Insights can identify IP addresses that deviate significantly from normal patterns. This makes it a suitable choice for the given requirement.

Hence, the correct answer is: SageMaker IP Insights.

Random Cut Forest (RCF) Algorithm is incorrect because this algorithm is primarily used for anomaly detection in high-dimensional data, such as time series or multivariate data. It’s effective for detecting anomalies in continuous numerical features but is not specifically designed for IP address analysis. While it could be used to identify unusual patterns in network traffic, it doesn’t directly capture associations between IP addresses and other entities.

Principal Component Analysis (PCA) Algorithm is incorrect because PCA is a dimensionality reduction technique that identifies orthogonal axes (principal components) in the data. It’s not specifically designed for anomaly detection or IP address analysis. While it can help reduce the dimensionality of features, it doesn’t directly address the problem of identifying anomalous IP addresses.

SageMaker AI K-Means Cluster Algorithm is incorrect. While K-Means can be used for simple anomaly detection by measuring distance from centroids, IP Insights is specifically optimized for capturing associations between IPv4 addresses and entities.

A data scientist working with Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is required to incorporate a new feature into an existing feature group that contains historical data. The feature group is designed to support several machine learning models. The data scientist must ensure that the new feature is added and that all records, including historical ones, reflect this new feature.

Which two actions should the data scientist perform? (Select TWO.)


Apply the PutRecord command to update the records that are missing data for the new attribute.
Set the new feature as the primary key to update all records automatically.
Reindex the feature group to apply the new feature across all records.

Execute the DeleteFeatureGroup command to remove the existing feature group.

Utilize the UpdateFeatureGroup command to incorporate the new feature into the feature group. Specify the attribute name and type.
Incorrect
You can update and describe your feature group, as well as add features and records, through the Amazon SageMaker Feature Store API console. A feature group is an object that holds your data, while a feature describes a column in the database. When you add a feature to the feature group, you’re essentially adding a column to the table. When you add a new record to the feature group, you are filling up values for features that are associated with a specific record ID.



To modify an existing feature group in the Amazon SageMaker Feature Store, you can use the UpdateFeatureGroup command to introduce new features. This operation allows you to add additional columns (features) to the feature group, ensuring that the feature group can evolve as your data requirements change. After adding the new feature, you can use the PutRecord API to update the records within the feature group. The PutRecord API enables you to ingest or overwrite records, ensuring that the newly added feature has data populated across both historical and new records.

Hence, the correct answers are:

– Utilize the UpdateFeatureGroup command to incorporate the new feature into the feature group. Specify the attribute name and type.

– Apply the PutRecord command to update the records that are missing data for the new attribute.

The option that says: Execute the DeleteFeatureGroup command to remove the existing feature group is incorrect because deleting the feature group would only result in the loss of all existing records, including historical data. The requirement is to maintain these records while adding a new feature. Removing the feature group contradicts this objective, as it would erase the entire feature group and its contents. Instead, the feature group should be updated without deletion.

The option that says: Set the new feature as the primary key to update all records automatically is incorrect because setting a new attribute as the primary key would not automatically update all records with the new attribute. Primary keys are unique identifiers that cannot be easily changed or used to update records retrospectively.

The option that says: Reindex the feature group to apply the new feature across all records is incorrect because reindexing is simply not a valid operation in Amazon SageMaker Feature Store. You must manually update records using the appropriate commands, such as PutRecord, rather than relying on a reindexing operation.

A real estate organization aims to create an ML model with Amazon SageMaker AI to forecast housing prices across different cities. The dataset contains a significant number of records with features such as square footage, number of bedrooms, location, and year built. The data scientist must select the appropriate algorithm for regression-based predictions.

Which SageMaker AI built-in algorithm would be most appropriate for this scenario?

SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm
Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm
Convolutional neural networks (CNNs)
Linear learner algorithm
Incorrect
Linear models are types of supervised learning algorithms that help make predictions based on labeled data. In simpler terms, the model is given examples where each example has some features (like size, price, or age) and an outcome (like a house price or a category). For classification tasks, the model sorts data into categories, such as whether a house is expensive or not. For regression tasks, it predicts a specific value, like the actual price of a house. The goal of the model is to learn a straight-line relationship between the input features and the predicted outcome.

Linear Learner Algorithm

The Linear Learner algorithm is the most appropriate choice for this scenario. The Linear Learner algorithm in Amazon SageMaker is designed for both regression and classification tasks. It is well-suited for problems where the goal is to predict a continuous variable, such as housing prices, based on various features like square footage, number of bedrooms, location, and year built. Since the target variable (price) is continuous, this is defined as a regressor task, distinguishing it from classification tasks where the output is categorical.

Hence, the correct answer is: Linear learner algorithm.

Random Cut Forest (RCF) algorithm is incorrect because it is only used for anomaly detection, identifying outliers in a dataset rather than making regression-based predictions.

SageMaker DeepAR forecasting algorithm is incorrect because this is simply designed for time series forecasting, which focuses on predicting future values based on temporal data. While powerful for forecasting tasks, it is not the best fit for regression problems like predicting housing prices from a set of features.

Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is incorrect because CNNs are primarily designed for processing and analyzing image data, not structured tabular data like housing features. While powerful for tasks such as image classification and recognition, CNNs are not well-suited for regression problems involving numerical and categorical features typical in real estate datasets.

question: Chatbot RAG sobre PDFs en S3 con LLMs. ¿Que par de soluciones hace buscables las guias operativas para el chatbot?
options: Ingerir los PDFs en una base vectorial de Amazon OpenSearch Service, y crear una knowledge base en Bedrock con Titan Embeddings G1 usando los PDFs en S3
Convertir los PDFs a texto y guardarlos en Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, y transformarlos con AWS Glue hacia Amazon RDS
Extraer entidades y frases clave con Amazon Comprehend hacia DynamoDB, y transformar los PDFs con AWS Glue hacia RDS
Guardar los PDFs convertidos en Aurora PostgreSQL, y extraer entidades con Comprehend hacia DynamoDB
correct_text: Ingerir los PDFs en una base vectorial de Amazon OpenSearch Service, y crear una knowledge base en Bedrock con Titan Embeddings G1 usando los PDFs en S3
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - OpenSearch como base vectorial y knowledge base de Bedrock con Titan Embeddings G1.

El problema: RAG necesita almacenar embeddings (vectores) y hacer busqueda semantica por similitud sobre los PDFs.

Por que sirve: OpenSearch funciona como base vectorial para guardar y recuperar vectores de alta dimension por similitud. Una knowledge base de Bedrock con Titan Embeddings G1 convierte el texto de los PDFs en embeddings, habilitando busqueda semantica precisa.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Aurora PostgreSQL (texto plano): una relacional no esta optimizada para busqueda semantica por vectores.
  • Glue hacia RDS: crear tablas para texto es ineficiente y no da recuperacion semantica.
  • Comprehend hacia DynamoDB: guardar solo entidades y frases clave pierde contexto, insuficiente para respuestas RAG precisas.
Exam tipRAG = embeddings + vector DB. En AWS: Bedrock KB + OpenSearch (o pgvector). Relacional pura no sirve para busqueda semantica.

A logistics company wants to improve its internal support system by implementing a smart assistant chatbot to help employees quickly find answers to complex operational procedures and protocols. The company’s documents contain PDF files stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The chatbot will leverage a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) approach using Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate responses.

Which solution should the ML engineer use to make the operational guidelines searchable by the RAG chatbot? (Select TWO.)

Use AWS Glue to transform the PDF files into a structured dataset and store them in an Amazon RDS instance.
Use Amazon Comprehend to extract entities and key phrases from the PDF files and storing them in an Amazon DynamoDB table.
Create a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock using Amazon Titan Embeddings G1 with the PDF files stored in the S3 bucket as the data source.
Convert the PDF files to text and store them in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database.
Ingest the PDF files into an Amazon OpenSearch Service vector database.
Incorrect
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is a technique used in natural language processing (NLP) that combines the strengths of retrieval-based and generation-based models. It involves retrieving relevant information from a knowledge base and then using a language model to generate a response based on the retrieved information.

Amazon OpenSearch Service can be utilized as a vector database, which is ideal for storing and retrieving high-dimensional vectors needed for RAG applications. This enables the chatbot to efficiently search and retrieve relevant document vectors that contain the necessary operational guidelines.

Opensearch Dashboard

Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that enables developers to build and deploy machine learning models for natural language processing (NLP) tasks, including question-answering and information retrieval. Bedrock can ingest data from various sources, including Amazon S3 buckets, and create a knowledge base that can be used by the RAG chatbot to retrieve relevant information from the operational guidelines.

Amazon Bedrock - Amazon S3

In a RAG setup, the retrieval process involves querying the Amazon OpenSearch Service vector database with a natural language query, using vector similarity search to find the most relevant sections of documents. These retrieved document vectors are then passed to a large language model (LLM) for generating the final response. Similarly, the knowledge base created in Amazon Bedrock can be queried by the retrieval component to identify the most relevant operational procedures, which are then used by the LLM to craft a response. By selecting Amazon Titan Embeddings G1 within the Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Base, the system converts the text data into vector embeddings, enabling the RAG chatbot to perform accurate semantic searches.

Hence, the correct answers are:

– Ingest the PDF files into an Amazon OpenSearch Service vector database.

– Create a knowledge base in Amazon Bedrock using Amazon Titan Embeddings G1 with the PDF files stored in the S3 bucket as the data source.

The option that says: Convert the PDF files to text and store them in an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database is incorrect. While Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is a fully managed relational database service, it is not optimized for full-text search and retrieval tasks required by the RAG chatbot. Storing the converted text files in a relational database would typically make it difficult to efficiently search and retrieve relevant information for the chatbot.

The option that says: Use AWS Glue to transform the PDF files into a structured dataset and store them in an Amazon RDS instance is incorrect because storing the transformed PDF data in an RDS instance would require creating a table with columns to hold the text data, which can be inefficient and resource-intensive for large amounts of text. For a RAG chatbot, the primary requirement is to efficiently search and retrieve relevant information from PDF documents based on natural language queries. This is better achieved using specialized services like Amazon OpenSearch Service (vector database) or Amazon Bedrock (knowledge base)

The option that says: Use Amazon Comprehend to extract entities and key phrases from the PDF files and storing them in an Amazon DynamoDB table is incorrect. While Comprehend can extract relevant information from PDF files, storing only entities and key phrases in DynamoDB may not provide enough context for the RAG chatbot to generate accurate and relevant responses.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/what-is.html

question: En un flujo RAG, ¿cual es el rol de un modelo de embeddings como Amazon Titan Embeddings G1?
options: Convertir el texto en vectores numericos para habilitar la busqueda semantica por similitud
Generar la respuesta final en lenguaje natural a partir del contexto recuperado
Almacenar de forma duradera los documentos originales antes de indexarlos
Orquestar el pipeline de ingesta programando los trabajos de carga de datos
correct_text: Convertir el texto en vectores numericos para habilitar la busqueda semantica por similitud
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - convertir texto en vectores para busqueda semantica.

Definicion: un modelo de embeddings transforma texto en vectores de alta dimension; al comparar vectores por similitud se recuperan los fragmentos mas relevantes (la R de RAG).

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Generar la respuesta final: eso lo hace el LLM generador, no el modelo de embeddings.
  • Almacenar documentos: eso es tarea de S3; los embeddings no guardan los originales.
  • Orquestar la ingesta: eso corresponde a la knowledge base o a un orquestador, no al embedding.
Exam tipRAG: embeddings (vectorizar) - vector DB (recuperar) - LLM (generar). Titan Embeddings vectoriza, no genera.

question: Conteo de animales en imagenes de dron (detectar y ubicar multiples objetos por escena). ¿Que algoritmo integrado de SageMaker es el mas adecuado?
options: Object Detection (dibuja cajas y clasifica multiples objetos por imagen)
Semantic Segmentation (clasifica cada pixel de la imagen)
Image Classification (asigna una unica etiqueta a la imagen completa)
Object2Vec (aprende representaciones vectoriales de objetos)
correct_text: Object Detection (dibuja cajas y clasifica multiples objetos por imagen)
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - Object Detection.

El problema: contar exige detectar y distinguir varias instancias del mismo objeto (animales) en cada imagen.

Por que sirve: Object Detection dibuja bounding boxes y clasifica multiples objetos por imagen, incluso en escenas complejas, lo que permite contar individuos.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Semantic Segmentation: etiqueta pixeles por categoria, no separa ni cuenta instancias individuales.
  • Image Classification: da una sola etiqueta a la imagen; no localiza ni cuenta objetos.
  • Object2Vec: aprende embeddings de objetos discretos para similitud/recomendacion; no analiza imagenes.
Exam tipContar = distinguir instancias = Object Detection. Segmentacion no cuenta instancias por separado.

A wildlife conservation organization uses drones to monitor endangered animals in a protected reserve area. It needs to count individual animals accurately using drone imagery. The organization is seeking advice on the best Amazon SageMaker AI machine-learning model for detecting and counting animals in the images.

Which machine learning built-in algorithm is most suitable for this task?

Object detection algorithm
Object2Vec algorithm
Semantic segmentation algorithm
Image classification algorithm
Incorrect
The object detection algorithm in Amazon SageMaker is specifically designed to identify and locate multiple objects within an image. It draws bounding boxes around detected objects and classifies them into different categories, making it very useful for tasks where you need to recognize what is in the image and determine the exact location of each object. This algorithm is well-suited for scenarios that require counting specific items, such as animals, in drone imagery, as it can distinguish between individual objects even in complex scenes.

object-detection

Amazon SageMaker AI’s object detection algorithm uses deep learning techniques, such as convolutional neural networks (CNNs), to achieve high accuracy in identifying and localizing objects. It is pre-trained on large datasets and can be fine-tuned with your data to meet specific needs. This flexibility makes it ideal for applications like wildlife monitoring, where precise counting and detection are critical. By using this algorithm, organizations can automate the monitoring of large areas, significantly improving the efficiency and accuracy of their conservation efforts.

Hence, the correct answer is: Object detection algorithm.

The option that says: Semantic segmentation algorithm is incorrect because this algorithm only classifies each pixel in an image into different categories, providing a detailed map of where different objects or materials are located within the image. This algorithm is typically used in fields such as autonomous vehicles to identify road signs and medical imaging to segment anatomical structures.

The option that says: Image classification algorithm is incorrect. This option simply assigns a single label to an entire image, categorizing it based on the predominant features. Additionally, it works well for tasks like sorting images into broad categories but cannot identify or count multiple objects within a single image.

The option that says: Object2Vec algorithm is incorrect because it is a general-purpose algorithm primarily used for learning vector representations of objects, which can then be used for tasks like similarity search, recommendation, or clustering. Therefore, this algorithm is not designed for image analysis or object detection.

question: Entrenar deep learning con dataset masivo de video en un file system distribuido, requiriendo alto throughput y baja latencia con lecturas/escrituras intensivas. ¿Que almacenamiento conviene?
options: Amazon FSx for Lustre, file system paralelo de HPC/ML que se integra con S3 para entrenamiento distribuido a gran escala
Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) en modo Max I/O, que escala su throughput agregado con el volumen de datos almacenado
Amazon File Cache, cache administrada de baja latencia que acelera el acceso a datos ya leídos desde orígenes remotos
Amazon EBS io2 Block Express, volumen de bloque de alta IOPS y baja latencia atado a una única instancia de cómputo
correct_text: Amazon FSx for Lustre, file system paralelo de HPC/ML que se integra con S3 para entrenamiento distribuido a gran escala
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - Amazon FSx for Lustre.

El problema: entrenamiento distribuido con enormes volúmenes de video en un file system compartido que exige throughput muy alto y baja latencia con I/O intensivo. Varias opciones prometen rendimiento; el matiz es cuál es el file system paralelo de HPC.

Por que sirve: FSx for Lustre es un file system paralelo diseñado para HPC y ML: cientos de GB/s de throughput, latencias sub-milisegundo y se integra con S3, ideal para entrenamiento distribuido que muchas instancias leen a la vez.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • EFS Max I/O: es NFS compartido y escala throughput con el tamaño, pero su latencia por operación es mayor que la de Lustre; no alcanza el rendimiento del file system paralelo de HPC.
  • File Cache: ofrece baja latencia, pero solo acelera datos ya cacheados desde orígenes; no es el file system primario de alto throughput para todo el dataset de entrenamiento.
  • EBS io2 Block Express: da IOPS altas y baja latencia, pero es de bloque y se adjunta a una sola instancia; no es un file system compartido para entrenamiento distribuido.
Exam tipFile system paralelo compartido para ML/HPC de alto throughput = FSx for Lustre. NFS compartido general = EFS. Bloque de una instancia = EBS.

The current project involves training a deep-learning model using a massive dataset of high-resolution videos. Which of the following storage services will meet the requirements?

Amazon File Cache
Amazon FSx for Lustre
Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)
AWS Storage Gateway
Incorrect
Amazon FSx for Lustre is designed specifically for high-performance computing (HPC) and machine learning workloads. It provides sub-millisecond latencies and supports hundreds of gigabytes per second of throughput, which is ideal for training deep learning models with large datasets.



FSx for Lustre efficiently handles the high I/O operations required for processing high-resolution videos. It is optimized for both sequential and random access workloads. It can seamlessly integrate with Amazon S3, allowing for efficient data access and management, which is beneficial when dealing with massive datasets typically used in machine learning.

Hence, the correct answer is: Amazon FSx for Lustre.

The option that says: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) is incorrect. While Amazon EFS provides scalable file storage for use with AWS Cloud services and on-premises resources, it is designed more for general-purpose workloads rather than high-performance computing.

The option that says: AWS Storage Gateway is incorrect because it is primarily designed to connect on-premises environments to AWS storage services, providing seamless integration and hybrid cloud storage solutions. It is not optimized for high-performance computing or the specific needs of deep learning model training. Its primary use case is for data backup, archiving, and hybrid cloud storage scenarios.

The option that says: Amazon File Cache is incorrect because it is only used to cache frequently accessed data, which does not align with the requirements of continuous and intensive read/write operations needed for training deep learning models.

Select the correct AWS service from the following list for each task. Each AWS service should be selected one or more times. (Select THREE.)

Automate the entire process of training, testing, and deploying the models.

Compile the code, execute unit tests, and build the necessary artifacts.
(AWS CodeBuild)
Automatically release new versions of the models to various environments while avoiding downtime and handling the complexity of updating them.

AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed continuous integration service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready for deployment. It eliminates the need to provision, manage, and scale your own build servers. With CodeBuild, you can define your build specifications as a series of build commands in a buildspec file.



AWS CodePipeline is a fully managed continuous delivery service that helps you automate your release pipelines for fast and reliable application and infrastructure updates. CodePipeline automates the build, test, and deploy phases of your release process every time there is a code change, based on the release model you define.



AWS CodeDeploy is a fully managed deployment service that automates software deployments to a variety of compute services such as Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, AWS Lambda, and your on-premises servers. CodeDeploy makes it easier to rapidly release new features, helps avoid downtime during application deployment, and handles the complexity of updating your applications.



Hence, the correct answers are:

– Automate the entire process of training, testing, and deploying the models: AWS CodePipeline

– Compile the code, execute unit tests, and build the necessary artifacts: AWS CodeBuild

– Automatically release new versions of the models to various environments while avoiding downtime and handling the complexity of updating them: AWS CodeDeploy

question: Se despliega un modelo XGBoost nuevo enviando un pequeno porcentaje del trafico al nuevo mientras la mayoria sigue con el viejo, para vigilar y poder revertir. ¿Que estrategia es?
options: Canary deployment (enruta un subconjunto pequeno al nuevo modelo y monitorea)
Blue/green deployment (cambia todo el trafico de golpe tras probar)
Linear deployment (desplaza trafico de forma gradual y constante)
Shadow deployment (corre el nuevo en paralelo sin afectar trafico real)
correct_text: Canary deployment (enruta un subconjunto pequeno al nuevo modelo y monitorea)
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - Canary deployment.

El problema: validar el nuevo modelo a pequeña escala con trafico real y poder revertir si hay problemas.

Por que sirve: el canary despliega la nueva version a un subconjunto pequeño del trafico real, permite monitorear metricas y detectar problemas temprano antes de un rollout total.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Blue/green: cambia TODO el trafico de golpe del viejo (blue) al nuevo (green); no es fase inicial pequeña.
  • Linear: desplaza trafico gradual y constante, pero sin la fase inicial de evaluacion a escala minima del canary.
  • Shadow: corre el nuevo en paralelo con copias del trafico, sin servir predicciones reales a usuarios.
Exam tipCanary = arranque pequeño. Linear = incremento parejo. Blue/green = switch total. Shadow = espejo sin impacto.

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
An ML Specialist is deploying an updated XGBoost machine learning model to detect fraudulent transactions. To minimize disruption and ensure a smooth rollout, the specialist begins by deploying the new model to a small percentage of transactions while continuing to process the majority with the old model.

What deployment strategy must the specialist use to ensure a controlled and safe transition?

Blue/green deployment
Linear deployment
Canary deployment
Shadow deployment
Incorrect
Canary deployment is a method that allows you to deploy new versions of machine learning models or applications to a small subset of users or traffic. At the same time, the majority continues to use the existing version. This deployment strategy enables you to monitor the performance and behavior of the new version on a limited scale, minimizing the risk of widespread issues. By observing metrics and feedback from the canary deployment, you can identify potential problems early and make adjustments before rolling out the new version to the entire user base. This approach is beneficial for ensuring a smooth transition, as it provides the flexibility to roll back to the previous version if any issues are detected.



Canary deployments can be implemented using Amazon SageMaker for machine learning models. SageMaker allows you to deploy models in production using canary or linear deployment strategies, ensuring controlled updates with minimal disruption. With canary deployment, you can gradually shift traffic to the new model, monitoring performance metrics and making informed decisions about when to fully deploy the new version. This method supports efficient model management, reducing the risk of errors and ensuring that only well-tested models are deployed to all users.

Hence, the correct answer is: Canary deployment.

The option that says: Blue/green deployment is incorrect. This option involves switching all traffic from the old version (blue) to the new version (green) at once after full testing. This method does not align with the phased approach, where the new model initially handles only a small percentage of transactions.

The option that says: Linear deployment is incorrect. This deployment strategy gradually shifts traffic steadily from the old version to the new version over time. While this method allows for a controlled transition, it does not provide the initial small-scale rollout and evaluation phase that Canary deployment offers, which is crucial in the scenario to minimize disruption and allow for immediate rollback if issues are detected.

The option that says: Shadow deployment is incorrect because this just runs the new version alongside the old version for testing without affecting live traffic. This method is primarily useful for testing but does not involve processing a small percentage of live transactions with the new model.

 

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/introduction-devops-aws/deployment-strategies.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/deployment-guardrails-blue-green-canary.html

 

Check out this Amazon SageMaker Cheat Sheet:

https://tutorialsdojo.com/amazon-sagemaker/

question: Estrategias de despliegue - ¿que caracteriza al shadow deployment?
options: Corre la nueva version en paralelo con trafico espejo, sin servir sus respuestas a usuarios reales
Envia un pequeno porcentaje del trafico real a la nueva version y monitorea antes del rollout
Cambia todo el trafico del entorno viejo al nuevo de una sola vez tras las pruebas
Desplaza el trafico de forma gradual y constante del entorno viejo al nuevo
correct_text: Corre la nueva version en paralelo con trafico espejo, sin servir sus respuestas a usuarios reales
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - corre en paralelo con trafico espejo sin afectar a usuarios.

Definicion: el shadow deployment ejecuta la nueva version recibiendo una copia del trafico real, pero sus respuestas NO se entregan a usuarios; sirve para validar comportamiento sin riesgo.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Porcentaje pequeno de trafico real: eso es el canary, que si sirve respuestas.
  • Switch total de una vez: eso es blue/green.
  • Desplazamiento gradual y constante: eso es linear.
Exam tipShadow = espejo sin impacto en usuarios. Canary = arranque pequeno real. Blue/green = switch. Linear = incremento parejo.

question: Entrenamiento con datos sensibles que debe estar aislado de redes externas (sin acceso a internet durante el training). ¿Que solucion cumple el requisito?
options: Habilitar el modo network isolation de SageMaker AI en el training job
Usar el cifrado en reposo y en transito integrado de SageMaker
Usar SageMaker Canvas con un VPC interface endpoint para bloquear internet
Guardar los datos de entrenamiento en un bucket S3 cifrado con acceso restringido
correct_text: Habilitar el modo network isolation de SageMaker AI en el training job
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - habilitar el modo network isolation de SageMaker AI.

El problema: el contenedor de entrenamiento no debe tener acceso a internet durante el proceso (aislamiento de red total).

Por que sirve: el network isolation mode ejecuta los training jobs y modelos sin acceso a internet, aislando por completo el entrenamiento de redes externas.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Cifrado en reposo/transito: protege los datos pero no aisla la red; el contenedor podria seguir alcanzando internet.
  • SageMaker Canvas + VPC endpoint: Canvas es una interfaz low-code para construir modelos, no garantiza aislamiento de red del entrenamiento.
  • S3 cifrado con acceso restringido: asegura los datos en reposo, no impide que el entorno se comunique con redes externas.
Exam tipAislar de internet = network isolation mode. Cifrado y VPC endpoints complementan, pero no aislan por si solos.

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
A company is training a machine learning model on a dataset containing sensitive customer information. Due to data privacy regulations, the training process must be isolated from external networks.

What solution would meet the requirements?

Store the training data in an encrypted S3 bucket with restricted access.
Use SageMaker Canvas and configure a VPC interface endpoint to block internet access.
Enable SageMaker AI network isolation mode.
Use SageMaker's built-in encryption at rest and in transit.
Incorrect
Amazon SageMaker AI provides various security features to ensure the privacy and isolation of training data and models. SageMaker’s network isolation mode allows you to configure your training jobs and hosted models to run without internet access, ensuring complete network isolation.

sagemaker-network-isolation

To meet the requirement of isolating the training process from external networks, SageMaker’s network isolation mode is an effective solution. Network isolation mode ensures that the training container does not have access to the internet during the training process, thus fully isolating the model training from external networks. This option addresses both data privacy regulations and the need to minimize operational overhead.

Hence, the correct answer is: Enable SageMaker AI network isolation mode.

The option that says: Use SageMaker’s built-in encryption at rest and in transit is incorrect because this option alone is not sufficient to ensure that the training data remains secure and isolated from external networks. While SageMaker provides encryption at rest and in transit, it does not inherently isolate the training process from external networks. Additional measures are required to achieve network isolation.

The option that says: Use SageMaker Canvas and configure a VPC interface endpoint to block internet access is incorrect because SageMaker Canvas is just a low-code/no-code interface primarily for building machine learning models, and it does not provide network isolation capabilities. Additionally, while VPC interface endpoints can be used to restrict internet access, SageMaker Canvas won’t guarantee that the training process is completely isolated from external networks, as there could be underlying connections or API calls that still communicate with the outside world.

The option that says: Store the training data in an encrypted S3 bucket with restricted access is incorrect because this is crucial for securing data at rest but does not address the network isolation needed during the training process. Encryption and access restrictions typically do not prevent the training environment from potentially accessing or communicating over external networks.

 

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/mkt-algo-model-internet-free.html#mkt-algo-model-internet-free-isolation

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/interface-vpc-endpoint.html

https://tutorialsdojo.com/amazon-sagemaker/

question: Modelo de 2 GB con trafico impredecible (picos en horario laboral, casi nulo de noche/fin de semana); debe escalar solo y ser barato en reposo. ¿Que despliegue conviene?
options: Endpoint serverless de SageMaker AI SIN Provisioned Concurrency
Endpoint serverless de SageMaker AI CON Provisioned Concurrency
Endpoint real-time de SageMaker AI con auto-scaling habilitado
AWS Lambda alojando el modelo, cargandolo desde S3 en cada invocacion
correct_text: Endpoint serverless de SageMaker AI SIN Provisioned Concurrency
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - endpoint serverless SIN Provisioned Concurrency.

El problema: trafico intermitente con periodos ociosos y necesidad de minimizar costo cuando no hay demanda.

Por que sirve: Serverless Inference escala automaticamente y solo cobra por la duracion de la inferencia y los datos, no por tiempo ocioso; sin Provisioned Concurrency tolera cold starts pero es lo mas barato para trafico intermitente.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Serverless CON Provisioned Concurrency: reserva capacidad siempre lista, lo que sube el costo en periodos ociosos.
  • Real-time con auto-scaling: mantiene instancias corriendo aun sin trafico, caro en reposo.
  • Lambda cargando el modelo: aunque una imagen de contenedor de Lambda admite hasta 10 GB (el modelo de 2 GB cabe), Lambda no es un servicio de inferencia ML administrado: cargar 2 GB desde S3 en cada invocacion provoca cold starts largos y latencia, tiene timeout de 15 min y factura por duracion, lo que lo hace ineficiente y no "fully managed" para servir el modelo.
Exam tipTrafico intermitente y barato en reposo = Serverless Inference. Provisioned Concurrency = quitar cold start pero pagar reserva.

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
A logistics company relies on a 2 GB custom machine learning model hosted in an on-premises environment to forecast delivery times. The company needs to migrate this model to AWS to lower operational overhead and use a fully managed service. The model experiences unpredictable traffic with peak loads during business hours and low activity at night and on weekends. The solution must scale automatically based on demand and be cost-effective during idle times.

Which AWS service is the most suitable for these requirements?

Use Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints with auto-scaling enabled.
Use AWS Lambda to host the model, loading it from Amazon S3 on each invocation.
Deploy the model as a serverless SageMaker AI endpoint without Provisioned Concurrency.
Deploy the model as a serverless SageMaker AI endpoint with Provisioned Concurrency.
Incorrect
Amazon SageMaker Serverless Inference is a purpose-built inference option that enables you to deploy and scale ML models without configuring or managing any of the underlying infrastructure. On-demand Serverless Inference is ideal for workloads that have idle periods between traffic spurts and can tolerate cold starts. Serverless endpoints automatically launch compute resources and scale them in and out depending on traffic, eliminating the need to choose instance types or manage scaling policies. This takes away the undifferentiated heavy lifting of selecting and managing servers.

sagemaker-serverless-inference-endpointWith SageMaker Serverless Inference, you pay only for the duration of running the inference code and the amount of data processed, not for idle time. This makes it a cost-effective option for workloads with intermittent or unpredictable traffic. You can easily create a SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint using the SageMaker console, AWS SDKs, the Amazon SageMaker Python SDK, or the AWS CLI. This allows you to focus on your machine learning model rather than managing the underlying infrastructure. Lastly, SageMaker Serverless Inference is well-suited for applications with unpredictable or intermittent traffic patterns, such as chatbots or other services that experience fluctuations in demand.

Hence, the correct answer is: Deploy the model as a serverless SageMaker AI endpoint without Provisioned Concurrency.

The option that says: Use Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints with auto-scaling enabled is incorrect. While SageMaker AI real-time endpoints can automatically scale based on demand, they are not designed to minimize costs during idle times. Real-time endpoints typically keep instances running even when there is no traffic, which can lead to higher costs during low-activity periods.

The option that says: Deploy the model as a serverless SageMaker AI endpoint with Provisioned Concurrency is incorrect because Provisioned Concurrency ensures that the model is always available, even during spikes in traffic, but this can only lead to higher costs during idle periods due to reserved capacity.

The option that says: Use AWS Lambda to host the model, loading it from Amazon S3 on each invocation is incorrect because the model size exceeds Lambda’s deployment limits.

 

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/serverless-endpoints.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/how-it-works-deployment.html

 

Check out this Amazon SageMaker AI Cheat Sheet:

question: SageMaker inference - ¿cual describe mejor el caso ideal del Batch Transform frente a un endpoint real-time o serverless?
options: Inferencia sobre grandes datasets de forma programada, sin endpoint persistente ni tiempo real
Inferencia bajo demanda sin endpoint dedicado, escalando a cero y cobrando solo por invocacion
Servir predicciones en linea 24/7 con instancias siempre encendidas, auto-scaling y baja latencia
Procesar payloads grandes de forma asincrona encolando las solicitudes en un endpoint persistente
correct_text: Inferencia sobre grandes datasets de forma programada, sin endpoint persistente ni tiempo real
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - inferencia por lotes programada, sin endpoint persistente.

Definicion: Batch Transform corre inferencia sobre grandes datasets sin mantener un endpoint vivo; ideal para trabajos programados que pueden durar minutos u horas y no exigen respuesta inmediata.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Bajo demanda escalando a cero: describe el Serverless Inference; tambien evita un endpoint 24/7, pero esta pensado para peticiones online cortas de baja latencia, no para procesar un dataset completo en un job programado.
  • Predicciones 24/7 con instancias encendidas: describe el real-time endpoint con auto-scaling.
  • Payloads grandes asincronos en cola: describe el Asynchronous Inference (endpoint persistente con cola), no un job por lotes.
Exam tipReal-time = online 24/7. Serverless = online intermitente, escala a cero. Async = payloads grandes en cola sobre un endpoint. Batch = lote programado sin endpoint.

question: Montar un Feature Store centralizado en SageMaker. Segun el flujo oficial, ¿con cual de estas acciones se arranca la configuracion de un feature group para retraining por lotes?
options: Definir un nuevo feature group
Definir el esquema clave-valor de un registro individual
Registrar los features en un catalogo de datos externo
Provisionar un online store de baja latencia para el grupo
correct_text: Definir un nuevo feature group
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - definir un nuevo feature group.

El problema: el feature group es el contenedor logico que agrupa features relacionadas y su metadata; nada puede definirse "dentro" de el hasta que el grupo existe.

Orden correcto: (1) definir el feature group, (2) conectar el offline store (historico en S3, para batch), (3) cargar/ingestar los registros por batch.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Definir el esquema de un registro: las definiciones de features (nombre, tipo, record identifier, event time) se declaran al crear el feature group; no es un paso previo suelto.
  • Registrar en un catalogo externo: el offline store del Feature Store ya se cataloga en el Glue Data Catalog automaticamente; no necesitas un catalogo externo aparte, y menos como primer paso.
  • Provisionar un online store: el online store (baja latencia para inferencia) se habilita como opcion del feature group; no aplica al retraining por lotes descrito y presupone el grupo ya creado.
Exam tipFeature Store: primero el feature group (define features y metadata), luego offline store (S3, training/batch) u online store (inferencia de baja latencia).

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
A financial services company uses 5 ML models to detect fraudulent transactions in real-time. The data team processes daily transaction streams for retraining to improve model accuracy. The company aims to create a centralized Amazon SageMaker Feature Store to organize and distribute attributes among different models and departments.

Select and order the correct steps from the list below to develop and distribute features. Each step should be selected one time or not at all. (Select and order THREE.)

Connect with an offline store to the feature group.

Schedule regular feature updates

Define a new feature group

Create an endpoint for feature queries

Connect with an online store to the feature group.

Load data into the offline store using batch processing.

Step 1:
(Define a new feature group)
Step 2:
(Connect with an offline store to the feature group. )
Step 3:
(Load data into the offline store using batch processing.)


Incorrect0 / 3 Points
Amazon SageMaker Feature Store is a fully managed, specialized service designed to store, share, and manage features for machine learning (ML) models. Features are the data inputs used by ML models during both the training and inference stages.

Feature group is the primary resource within Feature Store that holds both the data and metadata used for training or making predictions with an ML model. A feature group represents a logical collection of features that describe individual records. In the example diagram below, a feature group encompasses your ML data.

Offline store retains historical data in an Amazon S3 bucket. It is intended for scenarios where low-latency (sub-second) reads are unnecessary. For instance, the offline store can be utilized to store and deliver features for data exploration, model training, and batch inference tasks.



The correct steps to set up a centralized Amazon SageMaker Feature Store for managing features in machine learning (ML) models involve first defining a feature group, which organizes the features and metadata for model training and inference. Next, the feature group is linked to an offline store, which stores historical data in Amazon S3 and supports batch processing. Finally, data is loaded into the offline store in batch mode, enabling the company to efficiently manage and retrain ML models with updated features, improving accuracy and performance.

Hence, the correct answers are:

– Step 1: Define a new feature group.

– Step 2: Connect with an offline store to the feature group.

– Step 3: Load data into the offline store using batch processing.

The option that says: Schedule regular feature updates is incorrect because this option would be a separate maintenance task. Therefore, this is not part of the initial feature store setup process.

The option that says: Create an endpoint for feature queries is incorrect because this option is only related to querying features during inference, not part of the feature store setup for retraining.

The option that says: Connect with an online store to the feature group is incorrect. Online stores are typically used for low-latency access during inference, not for retraining models as described in the scenario.

 

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/feature-store.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/feature-store-concepts.html

https://aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/feature-store/

question: En el ciclo CI/CD, ¿que servicio AWS almacena y gestiona los paquetes ya construidos (con versionado, formatos npm/PyPI/Maven)?
options: AWS CodeArtifact (repositorio de artefactos y paquetes de software)
AWS CodeDeploy (automatiza despliegues evitando downtime)
AWS CodeBuild (compila el codigo y ejecuta pruebas)
AWS CodePipeline (orquesta el flujo build-test-deploy)
correct_text: AWS CodeArtifact (repositorio de artefactos y paquetes de software)
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - AWS CodeArtifact.

Por que sirve: CodeArtifact almacena, publica y comparte paquetes (Maven, npm, PyPI) con control de versiones; tras compilar en CodeBuild, los artefactos se guardan aqui de forma segura.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • CodeDeploy: despliega a EC2/Lambda/on-prem evitando downtime, no almacena paquetes.
  • CodeBuild: compila y prueba el codigo, produce los artefactos pero no es su repositorio.
  • CodePipeline: orquesta las fases del pipeline, no guarda paquetes.
Exam tipArtifact = repositorio de paquetes (npm/PyPI/Maven). No confundir con S3 ni con ECR (imagenes de contenedor).

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
An ML engineer is overseeing the deployment of a machine learning (ML) project and aims to streamline the process of building, packaging, and deploying their code. The engineer wants to use AWS resources to manage various development lifecycle stages.

Match each AWS service with the task it best suits in the ML project deployment process. Each service must be selected only once. (Select FOUR.)

AWS CodeArtifact

AWS CodeDeploy

AWS CodeBuild

AWS CodePipeline

It helps to avoid downtime during deployment.
(AWS CodeDeploy)
Build and test the code.
(AWS CodeBuild)
Store and manage the built packages.
(AWS CodeArtifact)
Automate the build, test, and deployment workflow.
(AWS CodePipeline)

Incorrect0 / 4 Points
AWS CodeDeploy is essential for deploying machine learning (ML) projects. It provides an automated and efficient way to deploy ML models and applications across various environments. This tool allows for deploying updated ML models to different instances, such as EC2, Lambda, or on-premises servers, with minimal downtime and reduced risk of errors. CodeDeploy seamlessly integrates with other AWS services, enabling smooth transitions between different stages of the ML lifecycle, from development and testing to production. By automating deployment processes and managing version control, AWS CodeDeploy ensures that the latest model updates are consistently and reliably applied, thus supporting continuous delivery and operational efficiency of ML applications.



AWS CodeBuild is a service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages ready for deployment. It can scale and process multiple builds concurrently, reducing the time needed to build and test code. CodeBuild is used to build and test code. Developers can configure CodeBuild to automate the process of compiling code and running tests, ensuring the code is ready for production before deployment.



AWS CodeArtifact is a service for storing, publishing, and sharing software packages used in development. It supports various package formats such as Maven, npm, and PyPI. This service is used to store and manage built packages. Once CodeBuild compiles the code, the resulting artifacts can be securely stored and shared in CodeArtifact while maintaining different versions.



AWS CodePipeline is a service that facilitates continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD) for quick and dependable updates to applications and infrastructure. It automates the release process’s build, test, and deploy phases and orchestrates the CI/CD pipeline. CodePipeline streamlines the workflow for building, testing, and deploying code changes, guaranteeing a seamless and automated process from development to production.



Various AWS services are essential in managing the code lifecycle when deploying a machine learning project. AWS CodeDeploy helps users to minimize downtime and reduce the risk of errors when deploying the ML models. AWS CodeBuild handles building and testing the code, ensuring it is production-ready. AWS CodeArtifact stores and manages the built packages, making them available for deployment. Finally, AWS CodePipeline orchestrates the entire CI/CD workflow, automating the build, test, and deployment stages to streamline the release process. Together, these services enable a seamless and efficient approach to deploying ML projects into production.

Hence, the correct answers are:

– It helps to avoid downtime during deployment: AWS CodeDeploy 

– Build and test the code: AWS CodeBuild 

– Store and manage the built packages: AWS CodeArtifact 

– Automate the build, test, and deployment workflow: AWS CodePipeline

 

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/welcome.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/govcloud-us/latest/UserGuide/govcloud-acp.html

question: Dataset sensible en un bucket de S3 en la region us-east-1, pero las instancias de entrenamiento de SageMaker corren en una VPC de us-west-2 (otra region). El trafico hacia S3 NO debe exponerse a internet publico en ningun momento, sin duplicar los datos ni cambiar de servicio de transferencia. ¿Que solucion aporta el acceso privado entre regiones?
options: Deshabilitar el acceso directo a internet y crear un interface endpoint (PrivateLink) en la VPC hacia S3
Deshabilitar el acceso directo a internet y crear un gateway endpoint en la VPC para comunicarse con S3
Replicar los datos con S3 Cross-Region Replication y entrenar el modelo en una copia local
Usar AWS Transfer Family para transferir los datos mediante SFTP seguro antes de entrenar
correct_text: Deshabilitar el acceso directo a internet y crear un interface endpoint (PrivateLink) en la VPC hacia S3
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - interface endpoint (PrivateLink) en la VPC hacia S3, sin internet directo.

El problema: el training job en us-west-2 debe alcanzar un bucket de S3 en us-east-1 (OTRA region) sin que el trafico salga a internet publico, sin duplicar los datos y sin cambiar de servicio.

Por que sirve: un interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) crea una ENI con IP privada en tus subredes; combinado con conectividad entre regiones (VPC peering o Transit Gateway) permite que SageMaker en us-west-2 llegue de forma privada al S3 de us-east-1, sin internet gateway ni NAT. Es la unica de las 4 opciones que da acceso privado cross-region sin duplicar datos ni cambiar de servicio.

Por que un gateway endpoint NO basta aqui: el gateway endpoint es intra-region y se aplica solo por la tabla de rutas de la VPC hacia el S3 de su propia region. Como el bucket vive en otra region (us-east-1) que la VPC (us-west-2), un gateway endpoint no puede alcanzarlo; ademas no ofrece IP privada/ENI ni acceso desde otra VPC.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Gateway endpoint: es intra-region (solo alcanza el S3 de la propia region via tabla de rutas); con el bucket en us-east-1 y la VPC en us-west-2 no puede llegar, y ademas no da IP privada/ENI ni acceso cross-region.
  • Cross-Region Replication: duplica el dataset (mas costo, storage y tiempo); el requisito es acceder de forma segura, no replicar.
  • AWS Transfer Family (SFTP): es transferencia de archivos, no integra con SageMaker para acceso privado durante el entrenamiento.
Exam tipGateway = ruta, gratis, S3/DynamoDB, intra-region. Interface (PrivateLink) = ENI/IP privada, muchos servicios, admite on-prem y otra VPC-region via peering/TGW. Ambos endpoints son regionales.
Linksdocs.aws interface vpc endpoint

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
An international banking corporation is developing a machine learning model using Amazon SageMaker. The training dataset contains sensitive financial data and is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 region. SageMaker instances in the us-west-2 region are required for training. The company mandates that the data transfer between regions must be secure, ensuring no exposure to the public internet at any stage.

What solution best satisfies these requirements?

Ensure the direct internet access feature is disabled for the SageMaker instances. Establish an interface endpoint within the VPC to securely connect to Amazon S3.
Configure SageMaker instances to operate without direct internet access. Set up a gateway endpoint within the VPC for secure communication with Amazon S3.
Use AWS Transfer Family to securely transfer the data between the regions using SFTP.
Use Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication to securely replicate data to the us-west-2 region, then train the model in that region.
Incorrect
Amazon SageMaker is a service that enables developers to build, train, and deploy large-scale machine-learning models. One key feature of SageMaker is its ability to securely connect to data stored in Amazon S3 via VPC endpoints. By configuring interface VPC endpoints, users can ensure that all communication between SageMaker instances and Amazon S3 remains within the AWS network, avoiding exposure to the public internet. This approach is crucial when handling sensitive data, such as financial information, ensuring that data is transferred securely between AWS regions.



Interface VPC endpoints allow SageMaker to connect to other AWS services without needing an internet gateway, NAT device, or VPN connection. This makes the data transfer process more secure and reduces the attack surface, as traffic between the services remains private. In scenarios where data needs to be transferred across regions, an interface VPC endpoint ensures that the connection is private and secure, protecting sensitive data from potential threats. Organizations can meet security and compliance requirements by restricting direct internet access and using VPC endpoints.

Hence, the correct answer is: Ensure the direct internet access feature is disabled for the SageMaker instances. Establish an interface endpoint within the VPC to securely connect to Amazon S3.

The option that says: Use AWS Transfer Family to securely transfer the data between the regions using SFTP is incorrect. This approach only provides secure file transfer protocols such as SFTP, FTPS, and FTP for transferring data. While it offers secure file transfers, it is not designed to address the specific requirement of ensuring secure data transfer between SageMaker instances and S3 without exposing the data to the public internet. Furthermore, the AWS Transfer Family does not intend to integrate directly with SageMaker for training across regions.

The option that says: Use Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication to securely replicate data to the us-west-2 region, then train the model in that region is incorrect. This solution would unnecessarily duplicate the dataset, increasing costs, storage usage, and replication time. The requirement is to securely access the data in real-time from SageMaker without public internet exposure, not to replicate it, making CRR an inefficient approach.

The option that says: Configure SageMaker instances to operate without direct internet access. Set up a gateway endpoint within the VPC for secure communication with Amazon S3 is incorrect. This approach is primarily used to access AWS services such as Amazon S3 and DynamoDB within the same region. Since the scenario requires secure data transfer between different regions, a gateway VPC endpoint would not meet the cross-region communication requirement since it does not support it.

 

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/interface-vpc-endpoint.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-privatelink/what-are-vpc-endpoints.html

 

Check out this Amazon VPC Cheat Sheet:

https://tutorialsdojo.com/amazon-vpc/

question: VPC endpoints - ¿que diferencia clave hay entre un gateway endpoint y un interface endpoint (PrivateLink)?
options: El gateway endpoint solo soporta S3 y DynamoDB; el interface usa una ENI privada para muchos servicios
El interface endpoint tambien es gratuito y, como el gateway, se aplica por la tabla de rutas
El gateway endpoint da acceso desde on-premises via VPN; el interface queda limitado a la VPC local
El interface endpoint permite acceder a un bucket S3 de otra region por si solo, sin peering ni TGW
correct_text: El gateway endpoint solo soporta S3 y DynamoDB; el interface usa una ENI privada para muchos servicios
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - gateway solo S3/DynamoDB; interface usa ENI privada y muchos servicios.

Definiciones: el gateway endpoint se agrega a la tabla de rutas, es gratuito y solo soporta S3 y DynamoDB dentro de la region; no da IP privada ni acceso on-prem. El interface endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) crea una ENI con IP privada en tus subredes, se cobra por hora, cubre muchos servicios AWS y admite acceso desde on-prem u otra VPC-region via peering/TGW.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Interface gratis y por tabla de rutas: falso; el interface se factura por hora (y por datos) y funciona por una ENI, no por rutas; el que va por rutas y es gratis es el gateway.
  • Gateway con acceso on-prem via VPN: falso; el gateway endpoint NO es accesible desde on-premises; el que admite on-prem es el interface (PrivateLink).
  • Interface cross-region a un bucket remoto por si solo: falso; ambos endpoints son regionales; alcanzar S3 en otra region requiere VPC peering o Transit Gateway hacia una VPC de esa region.
Exam tipGateway = ruta, gratis, S3/DynamoDB, intra-region, sin on-prem. Interface = ENI/PrivateLink, IP privada, se cobra por hora, muchos servicios, admite on-prem y otra VPC-region via peering/TGW.
Linksdocs.aws vpc endpoints

question: Preprocesar texto (limpieza, tokenizacion, embeddings con TensorFlow/HuggingFace) desde S3 con minimo esfuerzo de gestion, disparado al subir datos nuevos. ¿Que trio de acciones?
options: Un SageMaker Processing Job para preprocesar y generar embeddings, una Lambda que lo dispare al subir datos a S3, y S3 Event Notifications con Step Functions
Desplegar un cluster ECS en Fargate para los scripts, usar AWS Glue para limpiar el texto, y AWS Batch para orquestar los jobs de embeddings
Usar AWS Glue para limpiar el texto, AWS Batch para ejecutar los Processing Jobs, y un cluster ECS en Fargate para generar embeddings
Usar AWS Batch para gestionar los Processing Jobs, Glue para limpiar el texto, y un cluster EKS para orquestar el flujo de embeddings
correct_text: Un SageMaker Processing Job para preprocesar y generar embeddings, una Lambda que lo dispare al subir datos a S3, y S3 Event Notifications con Step Functions
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - SageMaker Processing Job, Lambda como disparador y S3 Event Notifications con Step Functions.

El problema: automatizar el preprocesamiento de ML con el menor overhead, arrancando cuando llegan datos nuevos.

Por que sirve: el SageMaker Processing Job es administrado y trae soporte para TensorFlow y HuggingFace; Lambda lo dispara automaticamente; las S3 Event Notifications reaccionan a nuevas cargas y activan el workflow. Todo administrado, minimo mantenimiento.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
A company is developing a sentiment analysis model that processes text data from customer reviews. The company collects and stores these reviews in Amazon S3 buckets. The data preprocessing pipeline involves text cleaning, tokenization, and embedding generation using machine learning frameworks such as TensorFlow and Hugging Face’s Transformers. The processed data is then used for training and fine-tuning the model.
Which set of actions will accomplish these tasks with the MINIMUM management effort? (Select THREE.)

Utilize AWS Batch to manage and execute the SageMaker Processing Jobs for data preprocessing.
Deploy a custom Amazon ECS cluster on AWS Fargate to run the preprocessing scripts.
Use Amazon S3 Event Notifications to trigger an AWS Step Functions workflow for data preprocessing.
Create an AWS Lambda function to trigger a SageMaker Processing Job when new data is uploaded to the S3 bucket.
Use AWS Glue to preprocess and clean the text data and store the output in Amazon S3.
Create a SageMaker Processing Job to preprocess the text data, generate embeddings, and store the output in Amazon S3.
Incorrect
Amazon SageMaker Processing Job is a fully managed service that simplifies the process of running data processing and model evaluation jobs. By leveraging SageMaker Processing Jobs, the entire pipeline from preprocessing to embedding generation can be handled with minimal management effort.

SageMaker Processing Jobs are designed to handle tasks such as data preprocessing and transformation, which align with the requirements of this scenario. They offer built-in support for TensorFlow and Hugging Face’s Transformers and can directly interact with data stored in Amazon S3.

AWS Lambda can be used to automate the initiation of SageMaker Processing Jobs based on specific events, such as the upload of new data to S3. This ensures that preprocessing starts automatically without manual intervention.

Amazon S3 Event Notifications can trigger workflows or functions in response to events in an S3 bucket. Using Lambda in combination with SageMaker Processing provides a streamlined approach to handling data preprocessing tasks.

Hence, the correct answers are:

– Create an AWS Lambda function to trigger a SageMaker Processing Job when new data is uploaded to the S3 bucket.

– Create a SageMaker Processing Job to preprocess the text data, generate embeddings, and store the output in Amazon S3.

– Use Amazon S3 Event Notifications to trigger an AWS Step Functions workflow for data preprocessing.

The option that says: Use AWS Glue to preprocess and clean the text data and store the output in Amazon S3 is incorrect because AWS Glue is primarily designed for ETL tasks, requiring setup like defining schemas and creating crawlers, which adds unnecessary management overhead. SageMaker Processing Jobs are better suited for machine learning workflows, offering straightforward integration with ML libraries like TensorFlow and Hugging Face for preprocessing and embedding generation.

The option that says: Deploy a custom Amazon ECS cluster on AWS Fargate to run the preprocessing scripts is incorrect. While Amazon Elastic Container Service (ECS) and AWS Fargate can be used primarily to run custom containers, they are not the most suitable choices for data preprocessing tasks in this scenario. SageMaker Processing Jobs and AWS Lambda functions are more specialized and managed services for data preprocessing and machine learning workloads.

The option that says: Utilize AWS Batch to manage and execute the SageMaker Processing Jobs for data preprocessing is incorrect. AWS Batch is a batch computing service primarily used for running batch jobs on AWS resources, such as EC2 instances or ECS clusters. While it can be used to run SageMaker Processing Jobs, it is not necessary in this scenario, as SageMaker Processing Jobs can be managed and executed directly without the need for AWS Batch.

 

References:

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/welcome.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/processing-job.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html

question: Modelo que corre una vez al dia, el procesamiento toma 45 min y la prioridad es minimizar costo. ¿Que despliegue es el mas costo-efectivo?
options: Un job de SageMaker Batch Transform programado a diario
Un endpoint serverless de SageMaker con escalado a cero
Amazon EMR para procesar los datos e invocar el modelo
El ModelExplainabilityMonitor para agendar la inferencia
correct_text: Un job de SageMaker Batch Transform programado a diario
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - un job de SageMaker Batch Transform.

El problema: inferencia programada (1 vez al dia, 45 min), sin necesidad de tiempo real y con foco en costo.

Por que sirve: Batch Transform corre inferencia sobre datasets sin mantener un endpoint persistente; se paga solo por el job, evitando costo de un endpoint 24/7. Maneja trabajos de minutos a horas.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Endpoint serverless: esta pensado para trafico impredecible de baja latencia y rafagas cortas, escalando a cero entre picos; no para procesar un dataset completo en un job de 45 min.
  • Amazon EMR: es big data (Hadoop/Spark); mantener un cluster cuesta mas y no es para inferencia programada simple.
  • ModelExplainabilityMonitor: detecta bias/drift de explicabilidad en endpoints, no agenda ni ejecuta inferencia batch.
Exam tipJob diario/programado, sin tiempo real, barato = Batch Transform. Serverless = online intermitente de baja latencia, no lotes largos.
Linksdocs.aws batch transform

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
A retail company runs a machine learning model on a scheduled basis to predict sales, with data processing taking 45 minutes. It only needs to run once daily, and minimizing costs is the priority.

What is the MOST cost-effective solution for deploying this model?

Deploy the model using an Amazon SageMaker serverless endpoint.

Use the ModelExplainabilityMonitor to schedule the periodic inference.
Use Amazon EMR to process the data and invoke the model.
Implement the model for processing using an Amazon SageMaker Batch Transform job.
Incorrect
Amazon SageMaker Batch Transform is a feature that enables you to run inference on large datasets without needing to maintain a persistent endpoint. This service is ideal for scenarios where you need to process data in batches, especially when the task can be scheduled and does not require immediate real-time responses. Batch Transform allows you to use pre-trained models for batch inference, which can handle processing jobs that take anywhere from a few minutes to several hours or even days, making it suitable for long-running jobs like daily sales predictions.

Amazon SageMaker Batch Transform

In this scenario, the retail company needs to run a model once daily with a processing time of 45 minutes. Since the model does not require real-time interaction and runs on a predictable schedule, using Amazon SageMaker Batch Transform is the most cost-effective approach. It allows the company to avoid the costs associated with keeping an endpoint live 24/7, making it the best choice for minimizing expenses while still meeting the operational requirements.

Hence, the correct answer is: Implement the model for processing using an Amazon SageMaker Batch Transform job.

The option that says: Use Amazon EMR to process the data and invoke the model is incorrect because it is primarily designed for big data processing using distributed frameworks like Hadoop and Spark. While EMR can process large volumes of data, it’s not optimized for the specific use case of scheduled model inference, and maintaining an EMR cluster would likely incur higher costs than using SageMaker’s managed batch transform service.

The option that says: Use the ModelExplainabilityMonitor to schedule the periodic inference is incorrect. This tool is used for detecting bias and explainability drift in live endpoints, not for scheduling or performing batch inference tasks.

The option that says: Deploy the model using an Amazon SageMaker serverless endpoint is incorrect because SageMaker Serverless Inference is typically designed for workloads with unpredictable traffic that require low latency, with a maximum processing time of 60 seconds. Since the model in this scenario requires 45 minutes to process data, serverless endpoints are not suitable, making this option impractical and less cost-effective.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/batch-transform.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/batch-transform.html#batch-transform-large-datasets

question: Un endpoint de SageMaker con target tracking sobre CPU escala demasiado seguido, causando inestabilidad. ¿Que se debe configurar para resolverlo?
options: Un periodo de enfriamiento (cooldown) entre acciones de escalado
Incrementar el valor objetivo de utilizacion de CPU
Reducir el numero minimo de instancias
Usar una metrica distinta de CloudWatch para el escalado
correct_text: Un periodo de enfriamiento (cooldown) entre acciones de escalado
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - un cooldown period entre acciones de escalado.

El problema: el escalado se dispara con demasiada frecuencia (thrashing), sin dar tiempo a estabilizarse.

Por que sirve: el cooldown period define cuanto esperar tras una accion de escalado antes de iniciar otra, dando tiempo a la aplicacion para estabilizarse y evitando el escalado excesivo.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Subir el target de CPU: puede reducir escalados pero arriesga sub-aprovisionar (instancias sobrecargadas antes de escalar); no ataca la frecuencia.
  • Reducir el minimo de instancias: baja la capacidad base y puede provocar mas escalados, no menos.
  • Cambiar la metrica: ayuda si la metrica es mala, pero el problema es de frecuencia/tiempo, no de que metrica se usa.
Exam tipEscalado inestable/thrashing = ajustar cooldown period. La metrica no es el problema si el disparo es demasiado frecuente.
Linksdocs.aws cooldown

Category: MLA – Deployment and Orchestration of ML Workflows
An ML engineer oversees a machine learning model deployed on Amazon SageMaker AI. To handle varying workloads, the engineer decided to implement automatic scaling. They configured a target tracking scaling policy to adjust the number of instances based on the average CPU utilization. However, the engineer noticed that the scaling actions were occurring too frequently, leading to instability in the application.

Which of the following options must be configured to resolve the issue?

Use a different CloudWatch metric for scaling.
Set a cooldown period between scaling actions.
Increase the target value for CPU utilization.
Decrease the minimum number of instances.
Incorrect
A hosted model in Amazon SageMaker AI can be set up to automatically scale (auto scale) based on changes in your workload. When the workload increases, auto-scaling adds more instances to handle the increased demand. Conversely, auto-scaling removes unnecessary instances when the workload decreases to avoid paying for unused provisioned instances.

Scaling Cooldown Period

A cooldown period is a setting that determines the duration to wait after a scaling activity finishes before initiating another scaling activity. By implementing a cooldown period, you can avoid excessive scaling, giving the application time to stabilize before making further adjustments. This helps minimize instability resulting from rapid scaling and allows the system sufficient time to adapt to the new capacity.

Hence, the correct answer is: Set a cooldown period between scaling actions.

The option that says: Increase the target value for CPU utilization is incorrect. Increasing the target value for CPU utilization typically means that the scaling policy will aim for a higher average CPU usage before triggering scaling actions. While this might reduce the frequency of scaling actions, it doesn’t directly address the issue of frequent scaling. It could also lead to under-provisioning, where your instances are overworked before scaling up, potentially impacting performance.

The option that says: Decrease the minimum number of instances is incorrect. Decreasing the minimum number of instances primarily reduces the baseline capacity of your application. This might lead to more frequent scaling actions as the system initially tries to meet the demand with fewer resources.

The option that says: Use a different CloudWatch metric for scaling is incorrect because using a different CloudWatch metric for scaling might help if the current metric is not a good indicator of the load on your application. However, this does not directly address the issue of frequent scaling actions. The problem of rapid scaling is more about the timing and frequency of scaling actions rather than the specific metric being used. Changing the metric might not solve the underlying issue of instability caused by frequent scaling.

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-prerequisites.html

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/sagemaker/latest/dg/endpoint-auto-scaling-add-code-define.html#endpoint-auto-scaling-add-code-cooldown

https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/application/userguide/target-tracking-scaling-policy-overview.html

https://tutorialsdojo.com/amazon-sagemaker/

question: Un equipo tiene scripts Python propios (con dependencias especificas) y quiere ejecutarlos en SageMaker de forma escalable. ¿Como incorporarlos?
options: Crear un contenedor Docker con las dependencias, subirlo a Amazon ECR y usarlo como processing/training container en SageMaker
Guardar los scripts Python en un bucket S3 y ejecutarlos directamente en SageMaker sin empaquetarlos
Crear una funcion Lambda con los scripts propios e invocarla desde SageMaker para el entrenamiento
Crear una imagen de contenedor para Amazon EKS y ejecutar alli los scripts de preprocesamiento
correct_text: Crear un contenedor Docker con las dependencias, subirlo a Amazon ECR y usarlo como processing/training container en SageMaker
answer_html:
Correcta: {{L}} - contenedor Docker en Amazon ECR usado como container en SageMaker.

El problema: ejecutar scripts propios con dependencias exactas dentro del entorno administrado de SageMaker.

Por que sirve: SageMaker soporta contenedores Docker a la medida; se empaquetan las dependencias, se sube la imagen a ECR (Elastic Container Registry) y se usa como processing o training container, garantizando el entorno exacto.

Por que NO las otras, una por una:

  • Scripts en S3 directamente: S3 es almacenamiento de objetos, no ejecuta codigo; hay que empaquetarlo en un contenedor.
  • Lambda: es para funciones cortas y sin estado, no para flujos de ML complejos ni entrenamiento.
  • EKS: Kubernetes agrega complejidad innecesaria; SageMaker trabaja directamente con Docker/ECR.
Exam tipCodigo/dependencias propias en SageMaker = imagen Docker en ECR (bring your own container).
